A1.justification: Both PDFs describe QPCert. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices support reliable comparison despite substantial reorganization and renumbering.

before.justification: v2 reports original certification experiments on Cora-ML, Cora-MLb, WikiCSb, and synthetic CSBM graphs, including architectural analyses and empirical attacks.

after.justification: v3 retains those experiments and adds original attack, baseline, halfmoon classification, and computational-scaling results.

M1.justification: The NTK/SVM equivalence, KKT reduction, big-M MILP, kernel-bounding procedure, and multiclass certification rule remain unchanged. Appendix O.2 presents structural certification as a prospective extension with unresolved optimization challenges.

E1.justification: Appendix O.5 adds the halfmoon dataset for non-graph MLP classification. The original graph datasets and four poisoning/backdoor scenarios remain. Larger CSBM graphs serve the added scaling experiment rather than introducing a different task.

E2.justification: v3 adds evaluated comparisons with DPA, GNNGuard, ElasticGNN, and AGT, plus MetaAttack-based gradients and Xing et al.'s backdoor attack (Appendices J.3, J.4, J.8, and O.5). The original architectural comparator sets are retained.

E3.justification: Added experiments introduce DPA partition counts of 5, 10, and 20; defense-specific training and tuning; four-epoch AGT evaluation; and runtime measurements on 1,000/10,000-node graphs with varied labeled-set sizes and 50 test nodes. Existing benchmark protocols remain substantially unchanged.

E4.justification: Existing architectural and connectivity ablations are retained. v3 adds backdoor certificate-tightness analysis, comparisons of attack gradients and backdoor strategies, DPA partition sensitivity, and a systematic study separating graph-size and labeled-set effects on runtime.

E5.justification: The original five-seed reporting, three seeds for Cora-ML, and standard deviations are retained. v3 additionally specifies ten seeds for defense tuning and three seeds for runtime measurements. These are experiment-specific additions, not evidence of increased runs for retained results.

E6.justification: Original result curves are retained, while Figures 10–14, 18, 28–29 add attack, baseline, and runtime findings. For example, Figure 29 reports positive QPCert certified accuracy at perturbation budget 0.02 where AGT reaches zero, under different network-width and training conditions. Figure 6 also gains a GCN heatmap.

T1.justification: v3 corrects the perturbation-vector norm from infinity to 2 in the l2 proof inequality (v2 Equation 24; v3 Equation 22). Appendix O.2 adds exploratory structural-poisoning formulations and a bilinear reduction. Principal certification theorems remain; the prominently displayed big-M proposition already appeared in v2 Appendix G.

C1.justification: The abstract and three introductory contributions retain the same claims: white-box poisoning/backdoor certification through NTKs and MILP, graph-architecture robustness insights, and applicability to kernelized SVMs. The rewritten conclusion does not materially change these contributions.

C2.justification: v3 substantially expands explanations of attack effectiveness, defense accuracy tradeoffs, and certification comparisons. It explains the MLP accuracy drop under transductive poisoning and adds detailed applicability limits concerning NTK equivalence, architectures, optimizers, structural perturbations, and computational scaling.

D1.justification: v3 adds previously missing architectural regularization values, DPA partition/test-node handling, MetaAttack adaptation, backdoor trigger settings, and defense hyperparameter grids. These substantially expand reproduction instructions. Code access is unchanged, while v2's explicit lowest-C cross-validation selection heuristic is omitted.

R1.justification: Beyond relocating existing related work, v3 adds substantive positioning against concurrent AGT, Li et al. (2025), a Lai et al. follow-up, and broader evasion-certification literature. Section 6 develops distinctions concerning certified models, threat assumptions, and applicability to node classification.

P1.justification: v3 reorganizes and expands the discussion, integrates and rewrites appendix related work as Section 6, rewrites the conclusion, introduces a symbols glossary, and relocates reproducibility information. These are substantial narrative and structural changes beyond the added experiments.

P2.justification: v3 adds comparison and runtime figures, expands Figure 6, reverses the panel order in Figure 9, and extensively reflows the paper into TMLR typography and layout. Existing plots are retained rather than replaced with revised benchmark curves.

improvement.justification: v2 provided poisoning tightness plots and rough runtime ranges. v3 adds backdoor and attack-strength validation, systematic scaling measurements, and external certification/defense comparisons, substantially strengthening evidence about QPCert's reliability and practical limits. Expanded applicability discussion improves scope clarity. Different models and threat assumptions limit DPA/AGT superiority conclusions, but the added validation still provides a substantial overall quality gain.
